By Dan Primack · Sep 17, 2026

⚖️ Situational awareness: The House yesterday voted to hold Leon Black in contempt, which could set the stage for federal criminal prosecution.

  • Black, the billionaire founder and former CEO of Apollo Global Management, recently refused to appear in front of the House Oversight Committee for a second round of questions over his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. He also refused to comply with a subpoena for copies of NDAs to which he's been a party.

🤖 You're invited: Ajay Agarwal of Bain Capital Ventures will join me on stage in Boston on Sept. 29 for our "AI Across America" event. Just yesterday, BCV announced that it's raised $1.6 billion for its 11th fund. Register here.

Top of the Morning
 

Illustration: Megan Robinson/Axios
 

Rivals are seeking to derail the $85 billion merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern, which would create the first U.S. carrier running coast-to-coast, Axios Pro's Colin Campbell reports.

Driving the news: BNSF last week said it will ask the Surface Transportation Board for access to 824 miles of trackage from Chicago to Harrisburg and Bethlehem, Pennsylvania.

  • CPKC and CSX, meanwhile, want access to trackager between Kansas City to St. Louis — arguing that Union Pacific's recent deal with Canadian National doesn't go far enough to restore competition.

The big picture: Union Pacific said in May that it would walk away from the merger if the STB grants such remedies, which would require it to pay a $2.5 billion breakup fee to Norfolk Southern.

  • And that's no small thing, given that Union Pacific reported having only $2.11 billion of cash and cash equivalents as of June 30.

Catch up quick: The deal was announced in July 2025 and is scheduled to close by early 2028.

Zoom in: None of the access asks are a surprise, nor are they guaranteed regulatory approval. It's also unclear if they're mostly about adding trackage or just backdoor efforts to scuttle the merger.

  • But they could put the STB in a bit of a political bind, given that Union Pacific has donated to the White House ballroom project.
  • The STB could approve both the access requests and the merger, hoping that Trump isn't digging too deep into the weeds (i.e., merger approval = good).
  • But if Union Pacific complains to the administration, let alone follows through on its threat to bail, then there could be blowback.

Look ahead: The formal access asks are due by mid-November, with the STB expected to rule sometime next year.
 
 
The BFD
 

Illustration: Rebecca Zisser/Axios
 

Siguler Guff & Co. has raised more than $3 billion for its sixth small-cap buyout fund.

Why it's the BFD: It's a reminder that there's big money in small deals, despite our tendency to focus on larger transactions.

Behind the scenes: The fund already is around 50% committed, with a split strategy between funds-of-funds and co-investments. It's the largest such vehicle Siguler Guff has ever raised, with expectations that the portfolio will be a bit larger than predecessors but that most of the excess cash will be used to increase ownership positions.

The bottom line: Small-cap buyouts are being driven by three main factors:

  1. There are hundreds of thousands of possible targets (i.e., most American businesses); usually companies held by families or founders that have never raised institutional capital.
  2. Such deals use relatively little leverage, which is a net positive as rates rise.
  3. There's a glut of midmarket fund capital, which creates exit opportunities once companies have grown (either organically or inorganically).

• TypeSafe AI, an SF-based composable AI startup led by OpenAI vet Diogo Almeida, raised $40m in seed funding led by DCVC. axios.link/3ViVy4J

• Comp AI, a security and compliance platform, raised $34m led by Roo Capital and Grand Ventures. axios.link/4izAWii

• Adaptive, a provider of accounting software to construction contractors, has raised $30m in Series B funding, per Axios Pro. Tidemark led, joined by insiders a16z, Emergence Capital, Pathlight, Definition, and 3KVC. axios.link/4xZfbx3

🚑 Altis Labs, a Canadian provider of AI software for drug development, raised US$25m in Series A funding, per Axios Pro. OrbiMed and Qiming Venture Partners USA led, joined by Innovation Endeavors, Benchstrength, Fusion Fund, and Cancer Breakthrough Fund. axios.link/4yBg9Q6

🚑 Polyphron, an NYC-based developer of human tissue models for drug development, raised $20m in seed funding, per Axios Pro. Quiet Capital led, joined by Gradient, Haystack, and Compound. axios.link/3VzyLBK

• Magentic, a London-based agentic platform for procurement data, raised $18m in Series A funding, per Axios Pro. Felicis led, joined by insiders Sequoia Capital and Westly Group. axios.link/46ymmAr

• Treble Technologies, a Reykjavik, Iceland-based developer of acoustic simulation for physical AI, raised $18m in Series A extension funding, per Axios Pro. Paladin Capital Group led, joined by insiders Kompas VC, Frumtak Ventures, and the EIC Fund. axios.link/4xyTfrI

⚡ R3 Lithium, a Covington, Ga.-based battery recycling startup, raised $15m from TDK Ventures, Integral GlobalTech Partners, and Axial Partners. axios.link/3UZTcrk

• Tare, an NYC-based blockchain credit exchange, raised $13.25m in seed funding. Blockchain Capital led, joined by Strobe Ventures, Janus Henderson, Apollo Global Management, The Venture Dept, Neoclassic Capital, and Avalanche Foundation. axios.link/4hawwvZ

• MicroLub, a U.K. developer of protein-based ingredients, raised $10m led by Northern Gritstone. axios.link/472u85L

⚽ Clearlake Capital Group purchased minority stakes in soccer club Chelsea F.C. from Mark Walter and Todd Boehly. axios.link/4cLB7n1

Public Offerings
 

⚡ Holtec, a Jupiter, Fla.-based nuclear power engineering company, postponed an IPO that was scheduled to price this week, citing "market conditions." It had planned to sell 50m shares at $15-$18, giving it a $9.35b market cap at the midpoint, and list on the Nasdaq (HNUC). axios.link/4xW1Vt9

• Haymaker Acquisition V, a SPAC led by Christopher Bradley (Mistral Equity), raised $250m in its IPO. axios.link/4hUvpm5
 
 
Liquidity Events
 

⚡ Apollo ‌is exploring strategic options for Energos, a floating liquefied natural gas infrastructure firm that could fetch more than $3b, per Reuters. axios.link/4hya29u

• Blackstone hired Goldman Sachs to sell the Asian business of U.K. events organizer Clarion Events, per Bloomberg. axios.link/470RJ6P

(Nasdaq: ACGCW), a SPAC affiliated with Atlas Credit Partners.
